# Sunday Serif (full reference)

> A soft serif for slow days. Free and open-source (SIL Open Font License 1.1), with print effects on variable axes. Made for Sunday (https://joinsunday.co). Roman and italic, a weight axis from 400 to 600 and three print effects as variable axes. Soft serifs, round terminals, a single-storey a.

- Weight axis `wght` 400 to 600, with named instances Regular (400), Medium (500) and SemiBold (600). Italic is a separate file per build.
- Effect axes: `BURN` Light Burn (0 to 100, default 0: towards 100 the ink floods the letters, like an overexposed print), `INKB` Ink Bleed (0 to 100), `WORN` Worn Print (0 to 100). At 0 the type is the clean print.
- Three web builds, each roman + italic variable WOFF2:
  - Text, family "Sunday Serif": SundaySerifText-Variable.woff2, SundaySerifText-Italic-Variable.woff2, about 55 KB each, `wght` only. Use it for text and preload it.
  - FX, family "Sunday Serif FX": SundaySerif-Variable.woff2, SundaySerif-Italic-Variable.woff2, about 1.8 MB each, all four axes. Load it only where effects show.
  - Grain, family "Sunday Serif Grain": SundaySerifGrain-Variable.woff2, SundaySerifGrain-Italic-Variable.woff2, about 1.5 MB each, one axis `GRAN` Grain Blur (0 to 100). A display cut: a blur made of grain, a cloud of ink dots spreading from every edge towards 100. Regular weight only.
- Desktop formats: OTF and TTF statics (Regular, Italic, Medium, Medium Italic, SemiBold, SemiBold Italic) and variable TTF, for Figma, Keynote, Word, InDesign.
- Character set: Basic Latin, Latin-1 Supplement, Latin Extended-A (Western and Central European languages).
- Downloads: one zip per release (SundaySerif-X.Y.Z.zip) with SHA256SUMS.txt. Sources (designspace and UFO) are in the repository.
- npm: the `sunday-serif` package ships the web fonts, `text.css`, `fx.css`, `grain.css` and `sunday-serif/next` for next/font.

## CSS

```css
@font-face { font-family: "Sunday Serif"; src: url("SundaySerifText-Variable.woff2") format("woff2"); font-weight: 400 600; font-style: normal; font-display: swap; }
@font-face { font-family: "Sunday Serif"; src: url("SundaySerifText-Italic-Variable.woff2") format("woff2"); font-weight: 400 600; font-style: italic; font-display: swap; }
@font-face { font-family: "Sunday Serif FX"; src: url("SundaySerif-Variable.woff2") format("woff2"); font-weight: 400 600; font-display: swap; }
body { font-family: "Sunday Serif", Georgia, serif; }
.title { font-family: "Sunday Serif FX", "Sunday Serif", serif; font-weight: 600; font-variation-settings: "BURN" 15, "INKB" 20, "WORN" 15; }
```

## The effects in detail

- Light Burn (`BURN`): too much light on the plate. Towards 100 the ink spreads into soft, heavy shapes, like an overexposed print. Only the shapes change: the spacing stays the same at every value.
- Ink Bleed (`INKB`): ink soaking into cheap paper. Towards 100 the letters swell into soft, organic shapes; counters stay open and letters never touch. The spacing stays the same at every value.
- Worn Print (`WORN`): a tired press and a dry roller. Grain eats the edges, dust specks and starved patches open up where the ink did not reach, growing towards 100; spacing never changes.
- The axes mix freely with each other and with every weight and the italic. Leave an axis out and it stays at 0.
- Grain Blur (`GRAN`, family "Sunday Serif Grain"): a separate display cut, Regular and Italic. A blur made of grain: towards 100 a cloud of ink dots spreads out from every edge, dense near the letter and sparse further out, like a dithered photo. The spacing stays the same at every value; it does not mix with the other axes.

## Loading on the web

- Preload only the roman text file: `<link rel="preload" href="SundaySerifText-Variable.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>`.
- Declare the FX family next to the text one and use it only on elements that move an effect. With every axis at 0 the two builds draw the same shapes, so "Sunday Serif FX", "Sunday Serif" as a font stack falls back cleanly while the FX file loads.
- Animate an axis with a registered custom property:

```css
@property --worn { syntax: "<number>"; inherits: true; initial-value: 0; }
.fade-in { font-family: "Sunday Serif FX", "Sunday Serif", serif; font-variation-settings: "WORN" var(--worn); transition: --worn 1.2s ease; }
.fade-in:hover { --worn: 80; }
```
